findings.title: `fetch_estimate()` consumes a JSON shape the CLI does not emit
findings.description: `fetch_estimate()` parses the whole stdout of `mt data tick pass --estimate-only --json` at `scripts/cutover_304_first_purchase.py:152-163` and returns it unchanged. The real CLI payload is a `PassResult.to_dict()` document with `phases[]` at `src/manta_trading/data/tick/pass_contract.py:119-130`; the purchase fields are written into that phase’s `summary` at `src/manta_trading/data/tick/purchase_phase.py:161`. The existing 234 helper confirms this contract by reading `estimate["phases"]` and `phase["summary"]` in `scripts/cutover_234_checks.py#purchase_wants`. However, `judge_estimate()` and `_check_scope()` index top-level `summary["wanted_days"]`, `summary["requests"]`, `summary["verdict"]`, and money keys at `scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:196-205` and `scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:222-245`. On a real run this raises `KeyError`; `main()` reports “unexpected payload” and exits before the estimate, purchase, evidence, or final checks can work. The unit tests avoid this by mocking `fetch_estimate()` with a flattened dict.

findings.title: The full cutover rejects the real `estimate_only` verdict
findings.description: The cutover’s first and final estimates use `fetch_estimate()`, which runs `--estimate-only` (`scripts/cutover_304_first_purchase.py:83`, `:152-163`, `:290`, `:298`). For a plan with wants, `spend_guard.evaluate_spend()` sets `VerdictStatus.ESTIMATE_ONLY` unconditionally at `src/manta_trading/data/tick/spend_guard.py:266-269`, and `plan_summary()` emits that status as `summary["verdict"]` at `src/manta_trading/data/tick/purchase_plan.py:277-301`. `judge_estimate()` only accepts `nothing_to_buy` or `allowed` and rejects any other verdict at `scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:223-245`; `VERDICT_ALLOWED` is `"allowed"` at `scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:44`. Therefore every real full-cutover estimate with requests is rejected as `verdict estimate_only`; the script cannot proceed to buying. The `--estimate` path bypasses this by using `check_ceilings=False`, but that also means it ignores all `summary["reasons"]`, including non-ceiling refusals such as archive-space shortfall.

findings.title: The generated 30-day ceiling ignores unheld provider jobs
findings.description: `ceiling_command()` computes `cap_30d` from `planned + trailing` at `scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:88-97`, and `judge_estimate()` uses the same simplified sum for the 30-day check at `scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:231-241`. The production spend guard instead checks `trailing_total + unheld_total + planned_new` against `cap_30d` at `src/manta_trading/data/tick/spend_guard.py:232-249`, and `plan_summary()` exposes `unheld_jobs` at `src/manta_trading/data/tick/purchase_plan.py:294-299`. If Databento lists unheld jobs in the rolling window, the printed PM command can set the cap too low and the real pass will refuse; re-submits also need the guard’s `planned_new` semantics because their estimates are already counted in trailing spend. The new tests cover only clean trailing/planned arithmetic and do not exercise `unheld_jobs`.

findings.title: `--slice` is not constrained to a slice identifier and can redirect state/log writes
findings.description: `--slice` is validated only by `_nonempty()` at `scripts/cutover_304_first_purchase.py:201-204` and `:227-229`, so values like `../../tmp/x` are accepted even though they are interpolated directly into `start_file()`, `baseline_file()`, and `record_start_and_baselines()` at `scripts/cutover_304_first_purchase.py:99-122`, and into `log_path` at `:239-242`. `start_log()` creates parents and writes the path (`scripts/cutover_common.py#start_log`), so an accidental or malicious slash-containing `--slice` can create files outside `NOTES_DIR`. The tests only cover missing and whitespace slice values; they do not pin the numeric slice-id format the module docstring describes.

findings.title: Estimate tests pin a fabricated contract instead of the CLI’s real payload
findings.description: The new/changed tests build a top-level “summary” with `"verdict": "allowed"` at `test/unit/scripts/test_cutover_304_checks.py:60-87`, and the cutover tests replace `fetch_estimate()` with those dicts at `test/unit/scripts/test_cutover_304_first_purchase.py:143-145` and `:528-540`. No test constructs a real `PassResult.to_dict()` payload, reads the purchase phase from `phases[]`, or asserts behavior for the `estimate_only` verdict. This gives false confidence: the two FAIL findings above are both caused by the tests asserting a shape/status the production CLI never emits. Add a boundary test using the real nested JSON from `pass_to_dict()`/`plan_summary()` and an `estimate_only` case before the cutover can be trusted.

structured_findings.summary: `fetch_estimate()` consumes a JSON shape the CLI does not emit
The full cutover rejects the real `estimate_only` verdict
The generated 30-day ceiling ignores unheld provider jobs
`--slice` is not constrained to a slice identifier and can redirect state/log writes
